q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2 FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.beer = s2.beer AND s1.bar <> s2.bar GROUP BY s1.bar, s2.bar HAVING COUNT(s1.beer) < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM serves WHERE bar = s2.bar)
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT s1.bar AS bar1, s2.bar AS bar2 FROM serves AS s1 JOIN serves AS s2 ON s1.beer = s2.beer AND s1.bar <> s2.bar GROUP BY s1.bar, s2.bar HAVING COUNT(s1.beer) < (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM serves WHERE bar = s2.bar)
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('B1', 'Address1'), ('B2', 'Address2'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('X', 'BrewerX'), ('Y', 'BrewerY'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('B1', 'X', 1.00), ('B2', 'X', 1.00), ('B2', 'Y', 1.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve a unique beer (no other bar serves the same beer) and another bar that serves a beer not served by the first bar. Q2 checks for pairs of bars that serve the same beer and have a count of the first bar's beer servings less than the total count of the second bar's beer servings.
counterexample_dsp: Consider two bars, B1 and B2, where B1 serves beer X and no other beer, and B2 serves beer X and beer Y. B1 should be in the result of Q1, but not in the result of Q2.
